clue.text: Man in charge during a period of minority rule

definitions.text: Man in charge during a period of minority rule

parts.words: Man in charge during a period of minority rule
parts.note: minority here means a monarch being under age, not a minority group in a population; someone governs on the child's behalf

explanation.definitionFit: When a sovereign is too young to reign, a deputy is appointed to rule in their name until they come of age.

clue.text: Sanguine porker grasping a 0 point

indicators.note: the porker is shown holding something inside it, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a porker is a pig, and a hog is a pig
a pin is a sharp point, as in a pinpoint

explanation.surface: An optimistic pig clutches something sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasping' is the container signal. The newspaper's text has a stray 0 before 'point'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sanguine means being optimistic, and an optimist is still expecting good things to come.

clue.text: Excellent conditions

parts.note: conditions read as what the sky and climate are doing outside, not terms of an agreement

explanation.definitionFit: Conditions can mean the state of the sky, so the best conditions are a fine sunny day.

clue.text: Where one might pray for eloquence of speech

explanation.definitionFit: A small chapel for private prayer has this name, and so does the skill of public speaking.

clue.text: I admit I may wrong if I speak thus

definitions.text: I admit I may wrong if I speak thus

parts.words: I admit I may wrong if I speak thus
parts.note: describes a polite phrase a speaker adds to concede that someone may set them right; the newspaper text drops 'be' before 'wrong'

explanation.walkthrough: The printed text reads 'I may wrong'; the setter meant 'I may be wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase is a speaker's hedge, conceding they may be put right by someone better informed.

clue.text: Make a song about the War Office on passing out?

indicators.note: the song goes around the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
WO is the usual abbreviation for the War Office, the old British army ministry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bursts into song about a government department while fainting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. Here 'passing out' means fainting, not graduating from a military academy.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, and fainting is losing consciousness.

clue.text: Frenzied tirade on restricted a supplies

indicators.note: something in a frenzy is wildly disordered, so the letters that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: An angry rant greets the news that supplies are being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenzied' rearranges TIRADE and ON. The newspaper text has 'a supplies', probably 'as supplies', which only adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are restricted in wartime are shared out in fixed small amounts per person.

clue.text: At a discount? Well, not entirely

explanation.definitionFit: Shares trading under face value are at a discount, and someone who feels slightly ill is not quite well.

clue.text: Fresh meat for a London borough

parts.note: fresh means new
ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: A butcher advertises fresh meat to a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: This east London borough contains Stratford, site of the 2012 Olympic Park.

clue.text: Help one gets in this day and age

indicators.note: the numeral one enters the other piece, so one goes inside another

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, labels the present era of dates
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.definitionFit: Help and assistance are synonyms, as in first aid.

clue.text: Small sum of US money sent round as a deposit

indicators.note: the word sent goes around the coin, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a dime is the American ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: A little American cash is posted off as a down payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal. 'deposit' looks like a bank payment but means what settles at the bottom of a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter that settles to the bottom of a liquid is a deposit, as silt is in a river bed.

clue.text: Amorous young Victorian hero about to turn in

indicators.note: the hero stands around the other piece, holding it inside his name

parts.note: Eric is the boy hero of the Victorian school story Eric, or Little by Little by F. W. Farrar

indicators.note: the little word to is turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: A lovestruck youth in a nineteenth-century novel is about to come to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the little word and 'about' is the container signal; 'in' is a link word. The surface hero is any boy, but the parse needs a specific Victorian schoolboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous feelings are sexual or romantic desire, and erotic describes the same arousal.

clue.text: The rules of play?

parts.note: play read as a theatre script rather than a game, so its rules are the directions to the actors

explanation.definitionFit: A drama script prints instructions telling the actors where to move and how to speak.

clue.text: A pound put on for service, perhaps

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pound is added to a bill for service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a restaurant tip but is a church service: a priest puts on this white vestment.
explanation.definitionFit: This long white linen vestment is worn by clergy celebrating the Mass.

clue.text: A drop in the ocean

parts.note: the idiom for a trifling amount is read literally, as the sea level going down

explanation.definitionFit: When the tide goes out the level of the sea falls, a literal fall in the water.

clue.text: What scandalised folk hope the storm will do eventually

definitions.text: What scandalised folk hope the storm will do eventually

parts.words: What scandalised folk hope the storm will do eventually
parts.note: the storm is a public outcry, which people caught up in a scandal want to pass and be forgotten

explanation.definitionFit: A scandal or squall that passes without lasting harm is said to subside and be over.

clue.text: Severe contest in which the B winners pull back

definitions.text: Severe contest in which the B winners pull back

parts.words: Severe contest in which the B winners pull back
parts.note: pulling back sounds like retreat, but in this rope contest the winning team literally hauls backwards

explanation.definitionFit: Two teams heave on a rope and the side that drags the other over the line wins.

clue.text: Soldiers ordered to hold an oil installation

indicators.note: the word for ordered holds the installation inside it

parts.note: bade is the old past tense of bid, so ordered
a rig is an oil-drilling platform

explanation.surface: Troops are sent to guard an oil platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' is the container signal; 'ordered' is an old past tense of 'bid', not 'arranged'.
explanation.definitionFit: An army formation of several battalions, so a body of troops.

clue.text: A 10 point cutter

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
a point of the compass, here east, E

explanation.surface: A tool with a ten-point rating is advertised.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodman's chopping tool is a cutting implement.

clue.text: A learner of French taken in by a showy performance

indicators.note: the French word goes inside the performance word

parts.note: a stunt is something done to attract attention
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French learner is fooled by a flashy act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' is the container signal, though it suggests being deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone studying at college or school is a learner.

clue.text: A question of the passage of time

definitions.text: A question of the passage of time

parts.words: A question of the passage of time
parts.note: describes an old idiom asking what o'clock it is, treating time as an opposing force

explanation.walkthrough: This dated British phrase was a jokey way of asking the time.
explanation.definitionFit: This old colloquial query, linked to the Duke of Wellington, simply asks the hour.

clue.text: Fuddled with gin she sounds equine

indicators.note: fuddled means muddled by drink, so the letters that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman befuddled by gin starts sounding like a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's cry is a whinny, so making that cry is sounding like one.

clue.text: Gets up witty sayings about United Nations

indicators.note: the sayings go around the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: bons mots are witty sayings, and mots alone is used the same way

explanation.surface: Diplomats put on a show of witticisms at the international body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; mots is French for words, borrowed in English for witticisms.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting up on a horse or a platform is climbing onto it.

clue.text: Sugared confection for those who arrive in good shape, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are to be said out loud and matched by sound

parts.words: those who arrive in good shape
parts.note: people who arrive in good shape come fit

explanation.surface: A sweet treat is offered to guests who turn up looking healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says COME FIT sounds like the sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat of a seed or nut coated in a sugar shell, an old-fashioned sweet.

clue.text: It rusted badly as the result of a landslide, maybe

definitions.text: the result of a landslide, maybe

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Metal corroded so badly it gave way, like ground in a collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges IT RUSTED. 'landslide' could be an election rout, but here it is literal rock and soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose fragments of rock and debris pile up after a hillside collapses.

clue.text: When he is around I make rapid progress

indicators.note: the word he goes around the letter I, so it sits inside

explanation.surface: Someone speeds up whenever a certain man is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to hurry or hasten along.

clue.text: Be back in time for a serious discussion

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: the short word be is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be home promptly for a weighty talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the short word and 'in' is the container signal. 'Be back in time' looks like an instruction to return punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument on a motion is a weighty discussion, as in Parliament.

clue.text: A youngster who has much to learn from the peony

definitions.text: A youngster who has much to learn

indicators.note: the answer is made from these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A novice gardener can learn a lot from a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals that the letters of THE PEONY are made into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or beginner, who is new to a skill, still has everything to master.
